title: The Best Travel Backpacks of 2025, Tested — PackVerdict
text: We flew 31 flights and walked 400 km with 14 travel backpacks. Best overall: Osprey Farpoint 40. No other pack matches its carrying comfort — the ventilated AirScape back panel and a real, padded hipbelt move the load onto your hips, and after a 12-hour travel day our testers' shoulders were the least sore with the Farpoint by a wide margin. Add the All Mighty lifetime guarantee and it is the safest $185 in travel gear. Best organization: Cotopaxi Allpa 35. The full clamshell opens flat with mesh-covered compartments on both sides; it is the only pack where we never used packing cubes. Security zippers and burly 1000D TPU shell are bonuses; at $200 and 1.6 kg it is neither cheap nor light. Best budget: Decathlon Forclaz Travel 500. Ninety euros buys a full suitcase-style opening, a separate shoe compartment, a removable waist belt and a 10-year warranty — astonishing value if you can live with the looks. Best for budget airlines: CabinZero Classic 36. At 760 g with a soft, squashable shape it slides into Ryanair and easyJet sizers that reject stiffer packs, and the $80 price is friendly. Be aware the padding is minimal and there is no hipbelt or frame, so keep loads light and days short. Bottom line: comfort-first travelers should pay for the Osprey; organization obsessives, the Cotopaxi; value hunters, the Decathlon; budget-airline minimalists, the CabinZero.
